newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslavia to increase wheat area, official says.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslavia to increase wheat area, official says.

text.p: BELGRADE, Sept 9 (Retuer) - Yugoslavia will increase the land planted with wheat by 250,000 hectares this autumn, a senior agriculture ministry official said on Monday.
"The plan is to sow 850,000 hectares with wheat, out of about 1.1 million hectares set aside for autumn sowing this year," Milan Prostran, undersecretary in the federal Agriculture Ministry said.

"This is an increase of more than 250,000 hectares compared to the area sown last year," he said. "This will almost bring us back to the level of the average wheat acreage over the past 10 years of 860,000 hectares."
Yugoslavia, now comprising Serbia and Montenegro, last year reduced the area under wheat by 300,000 hectares to 582,965 ha.
Its wheat harvest dropped to record low of 1.72 million tonnes, down from 2.97 million tonnes in 1995 -- and the lowest since 1963 when it stood at 1.9 million tonnes.

Wheat yields this year fell to 2.96 tonnes per hectare from 3.4 tonnes the previous year. The yield is at its lowest level since 1972 when it stood at 2.7 tonnes a hectare. --Gordana Kukic, Belgrade Newsroom +381 11 222 4254
